label: Get the Job — Sales Tracker
overview: The Get the Job — Sales Tracker is a spreadsheet-based sales pipeline and performance management system (Get.1a.Sales Tracker). It creates a transparent record of sales activities, pipeline velocity, referral networks, and team performance. Five primary worksheets cover the full tracking lifecycle: firm-wide macro metrics, individual team performance, prospect-level CRM activity, centre of influence development, and system configuration. Entry-level and suitable for any advisor focused on fee growth. Each worksheet is treated here as its own material, because each is used by a different person at a different moment.

diagnostic_entry.primary_question: Which area of your sales pipeline do you need to work on — tracking individual prospects, measuring team performance, managing your referral network, or reviewing your overall firm-wide conversion metrics?

materials.name: Tracker Configuration (Lists & Calcs)
materials.summary: The engine room. Lists holds the standardised dropdowns — relationship type, approach styles, meeting themes, prospect sources, Total Needs stages, staff names — which is what keeps the data clean enough to report on. Calcs handles the background statistics: averages, variances and standard deviations. Getting this right makes daily entry fast and uniform, and it is the reason the final numbers can be trusted for a decision.
materials.who_when: The system administrator or operations manager responsible for setting up and maintaining internal tracking tools. Done once, before the tracker goes anywhere near the team.
steps: Open the Lists tab before deploying the tracker to anyone.
Populate the exact team members, split into Partners and Staff Support.
Enter the standard meeting themes your firm actually uses — Lite Funda' Sales, Formal Risk Mgt, Planning Review and so on.
Enter the approach styles the firm uses, so conversion can later be compared style by style.
Leave the Calcs tab alone in normal use — it is what produces the averages, variances and standard deviations behind the reports.
Deploy only once the dropdowns are complete; free-typed entries are what destroy the reporting later.

materials.name: Sales Activity Log
materials.summary: A lightweight CRM: one row per prospect, holding contact details, current sales stage, proposal value and the next move. It is what stops a prospect falling through the cracks, and its Work Days Elapsed calculation is the early warning that a deal has stalled. For the firm it turns the pipeline into something visible and countable, with each lead carrying an honest status — Active, Await Research, Completed, Dead or On Hold.
materials.who_when: Daily use by every client-facing advisor, logging activity on the day it happens rather than catching up at the end of the week.
steps: Log a new row the moment an approach is made — prospect name, business name, lead staff member, prospect source, and the approach style used.
Update Prospect Status as the relationship moves: Active, Dead, Completed, and record whether a meeting was secured.
Enter the value in the Proposal Value column as soon as a proposal is requested, so pending revenue is visible rather than remembered.
Watch Work Days Elapsed — a deal sitting at 119 or 145 days is stalling and needs either intervention or an honest reclassification.
Where the prospect is simply not ready, set the status to On Hold or Await Research: they stay in the system for follow-up without inflating the active pipeline.
Where Work Days Elapsed passes 90 days with nothing secured, move the status to On Hold or Dead and move on. Keeping stalled prospects active artificially inflates the projection.
Record the specific follow-up note and date every time, so the next move is written down rather than carried in someone's head.

materials.name: COI (Centres of Influence) Development
materials.summary: Systematises the referral network by recording the relationship status with each external professional — bankers, lawyers, insurance brokers — and moving them deliberately through the trust stages: Could We, How Would We, then Will We test and review. It also quantifies what each relationship is actually worth, tying referrals, conversions and fee value to the individual COI, which is what tells an advisor where their networking time is paying and where it is not.
materials.who_when: Senior partners, business development managers, and advisors building organic growth through strategic alliances.
steps: After a networking event or coffee meeting with a professional such as a commercial lender or lawyer, add their details to the COI Development tab straight away.
Record the relationship stage and update the progress column (1 for yes, 0 for no) as trust builds.
Move the indicator from Could We to How Would We once they agree to explore a mutual alliance — relationships have to be nurtured through the stages before referrals can be expected.
Track the number of referrals given by each COI, and how many converted.
Record the closed fee value that originated from each relationship, so the return on the networking is a number rather than a feeling.
Review the ones that are not moving: a COI sitting at Could We for months with no fee value is a signal to redirect the networking effort elsewhere.

materials.name: Team Report
materials.summary: Breaks the firm-wide numbers down to the individual: prospects approached, meetings secured, proposals sent, and total value of work won per person. For the advisor it gives an undeniable read on their own average proposal value and win rate. For the firm it locates the training need precisely — an advisor who is excellent at securing meetings but rarely closes needs different coaching from one who cannot get the meeting at all.
materials.who_when: One-on-one performance reviews, team accountability meetings, and identifying top performers.
steps: Review each team member's approaches, meetings secured, proposals sent and value secured together — a single metric on its own misleads.
Compare average proposal value and win rate across the team to see who is strong at which part of the process.
Where an advisor shows a high number of approaches but an exceptionally low secured conversion, assign a senior partner as Support Staff (Buddy) on their next active prospect.
Use the pattern rather than the total to choose the coaching — meeting-getting and closing are different skills and need different help.
Run it monthly alongside the Stats to Date review.

materials.name: Stats to Date Dashboard
materials.summary: The macro view of the whole firm: conversion rates by approach style — direct contact against quiz link sent — and by prospect source, referral against social media. It shows which sales style is producing the higher average fee, Campaign or Total Needs, and therefore where the firm's time is best spent. It also separates existing clients from new prospects, which is what reveals whether growth is coming from upselling or from genuinely new business.
materials.who_when: Firm owners, managing partners and sales directors needing the firm-wide picture. Reviewed at the end of each month, alongside the Team Report.
steps: At month end, review the total value of work proposed against the value actually secured, and read the win rate from that.
Compare conversion by approach style — direct contact, pre-approach sequences, gifts, quiz links — and double down on whichever produces the highest percentage of agreeable prospects.
Compare Campaign against Total Needs on average fee value, to see which style is returning most for the time invested.
Read the relationship-type split: existing clients against new prospects tells you whether growth is organic upselling or successful lead generation.
Note how many meetings are actually required to produce one proposal, and use that ratio when planning activity levels.
Adjust the firm's sales strategy on what the tab shows, then re-read it next month to see whether the change worked.

advisor_guidance.daily_discipline: The tracker only works if it is updated daily at the point of activity. End-of-week catch-up entries are less reliable and miss nuance. Make it a non-negotiable habit: every approach is logged on the day it happens.
advisor_guidance.pipeline_hygiene: A pipeline full of stalled prospects is not an asset — it is noise. Review Work Days Elapsed weekly and reclassify stalled deals as 'On Hold' or 'Dead' promptly. A clean, realistic pipeline is more useful than an inflated one.
advisor_guidance.coi_vs_direct: Track both COI-sourced and directly-sourced leads. The Stats to Date dashboard will show you over time whether your referral network or your direct outreach is generating better quality prospects — and where to invest your BD time accordingly.
